answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by binding every identity to a locked stake that is slashed if two accounts ever share one behavioral thread. Provenance is recorded like a block of onyx: hard, unforgeable, and impossible to edit after the fact. When a falcon-eyed detector notices duplicate signing keys or shared compute fingerprints, it seizes the bond, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand deposits that never pay back. Fake identities become more expensive than the rewards they could harvest, and the attack collapses on its own economics.
